title: The First Cell From a Position That Is at Least x

concept.title: With maxima in the tree, a question can walk down to the leftmost block that has a large enough maximum
body: A row of numbers changes one cell at a time. A question gives a start position `x` and a limit `y`: **find the first cell at position `x` or later whose value is at least `y`**, or report that there is none. For the row `3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6` the first cell from the position 3 with a value of at least 5 is the cell 5. Scanning from `x` costs O(n) in the worst case.

Keep the **maximum** of every block in a segment tree. A block whose maximum is less than `y` contains no answer and can be skipped as a whole. Start at the leaf of the cell `x`. If this leaf is large enough, we are done. Otherwise move to the next block on the right: while the current node is a **right child**, go up to its parent (that block is finished); then step to the **right sibling** (the node `v + 1`). At the first node with `tree[v] >= y` the answer is inside it: **descend**, going to the left child if its maximum is at least `y` and to the right child otherwise.

Unused leaves hold a value smaller than every limit, so the descent never ends in them. The search skips whole blocks, so it takes O(log n) steps, the same as a change of one cell. This "walk on the tree" is what makes a segment tree stronger than a Fenwick tree for searching questions.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` asks for the smallest position `p >= x` with the number at `p` at least `y` (print -1 if there is none). Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.

Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the number of the first cell at position `x` or later whose value is at least `y`, or -1 if there is none.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.

examples.note: The first cell from 3 with a value of at least 5 is the cell 5. After the change the cell 3 itself qualifies: 5 3.

hints: Store the maximum of every block.
Skip a block whose maximum is below the limit.
Climb while the node is a right child, step to the right sibling, and descend into the leftmost good child.

explanation: The tree stores block maxima; a question starts at the leaf of x, skips finished blocks by climbing from right children and stepping to right siblings, and descends into the leftmost child whose maximum reaches the limit.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).
